standard_prerequisites.name: Half adjoint equivalence structure
standard_prerequisites.statement: The type of half adjoint equivalences on f collects an inverse, a homotopy and a coherence path between the two composites.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type shown to be a mere proposition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Being a proposition via contractibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: It suffices to assume the structure inhabited and prove the type contractible, by the standard criterion for propositionality.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction the proof opens with.

standard_prerequisites.name: Associativity of the Sigma type
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Sigma type whose second component is itself a Sigma type is equivalent to the flattened Sigma type over the two components.
standard_prerequisites.use: It rewrites the structure into a Sigma type over the right inverse type.

core_obligations: Assume f to be a half adjoint equivalence and reduce the goal to contractibility of the structure (source lines 363-363).
Rewrite the structure by associativity of the Sigma type as the Sigma type of right inverses together with the coherence datum at that inverse (source lines 364-365).

Use contractibility of the right inverse type and of the coherence type, together with the fact that a Sigma type over a contractible base with contractible fibres is contractible, to conclude (source lines 365-366).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce propositionality to contractibility of the structure.
Flatten the structure into a Sigma type over the right inverse type.
Contractibility of the two layers closes the argument.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 359-361 (book Theorem 4.2.13): for every map f the type of half adjoint equivalence structures on f is a mere proposition. The statement is a propositionality claim about a nested structure, and the proof (source lines 362-367) has to choose the right reduction: it first turns propositionality into contractibility under an assumed inhabitant, then rewrites the structure by associativity of the Sigma type so that the coherence datum is taken at the right inverse rather than at the inverse map, and only then can it invoke the two contractibility results and the closure of contractibility under Sigma types. Which component the structure should be flattened at, and why that is the right choice, is exactly what the statement does not show.
